name: Franklin Brandt
life: “I still remember the first night an entire ward slept.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Paper & Pine Books, where Franklin starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I wanted the noisy bearing replaced. Hearing the song hasn't changed my mind about my night shift.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an olive canvas jacket and a small enamel bird on the lapel. Franklin has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with close-cropped dark curls. Franklin draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
personality: Franklin carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To buy one quiet night before the next shift.
family: Lou Arnett is Franklin’s stepsibling. Franklin chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Lou brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The sheltered corner*, Lou says, “I set the distance in a planning office. My father made me walk it with his groceries.”
connections: Thomas Silva. The people trying to sleep get a say in when the morning choir rehearses. Also in the story is Alejandro Sanders (machine listener).

reactions.situation: The washer bearing goes quiet mid-song
reactions.response: Franklin listens for the missing note and lets maintenance know what changed.

reactions.response: Franklin keeps listening through the pause and lets the musician choose the next note.
